title: Semiautomated Longitudinal Microcomputed Tomography-based Quantitative Structural Analysis of a Nude Rat Osteoporosis-related Vertebral Fracture Model
protocol: Purchase six-week-old athymic ovariectomized rats.
Place the rats on a low calcium diet (LCD) containing 0.01% calcium and 0.77% phosphate for four months.
Switch the rats back to a normal diet after four months of LCD feeding.
Drill a critical-size vertebral defect in the fourth and fifth lumbar vertebral bodies (L4-L5).
Image the rats on day 1 post-surgery using µCT scans.
Reimage the rats at weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12 after defect establishment using µCT scans.
Locate the defect margins on the day 1 scan to define a cylindrical volume of interest (VOI).
Reorient subsequent µCT scans for weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12 to match the standard position defined from the day 1 scan.
Apply the predefined VOI from day 1 to the registered scans at weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12.
Assess bone volume density in the VOIs using µCT scans.
Evaluate apparent density of the VOIs using µCT scans.
Autoclave all surgical tools prior to surgery.
Sterilize all surgical tools in the case of multiple surgeries.
Wash the tools and place them in a sonicator bath for 5 min.
Place the washed tools in a hot bead sterilizer set to 250 °C for 20 s.
Allow the sterilized tools to cool down for 5 min.
Induce anesthesia using 5% isoflurane in 100% oxygen.
Maintain anesthesia via nose cone at 2 - 3% isoflurane.
Apply vet ointment on the eyes to prevent dryness under anesthesia.
Perform a toe-pinch stimulus to ensure adequate plane of anesthesia.
Initiate the procedure if no response is noted from the toe-pinch stimulus.
Place the anesthetized rat in dorsal recumbency on a heating pad set at 37 °C.
Stretch the limbs using a magnetic fixator retraction system.
Shave the abdominal area using an electric shaver.
Swab the shaved area with iodine-based antiseptic and chlorhexidine gluconate 0.5%.
Follow swabbing with 70% ethanol application.
Inject the rat with carprofen (5 mg/kg body weight, subcutaneous).
Begin the incision 1 cm below the xiphoid process.
Cut through the midline (~5 - 8 cm).
Use surgical scissors to make an incision through the linea alba to access the abdominal cavity.
Expose the abdominal cavity using retractors.
Deflect the intestines to the right to expose the abdominal aorta and left kidney.
Palpate the lumbar spine before proceeding to expose it.
Wrap internal organs with sterile gauzes soaked in sterile saline solution to avoid dehydration.
Use thermocautery to expose layers of lumbar vertebral bodies L4-5, isolating them from surrounding tissues.
Clean the exposed vertebrae using a sterile cotton swab saturated with sterile saline.
Drill a 5 mm-deep bone defect in the center of the anterior aspect of the vertebral body at L4.
Clean the defect and apply pressure to stop bleeding if present.
Repeat steps for drilling and cleaning on the L5 vertebra to create a total of two defects per rat.
Return the intestines to the abdominal cavity.
Use vicryl synthetic absorbable surgical suture in a continuous pattern to suture the aponeurosis.
Close the skin using a simple interrupted pattern with a 4-0 monofilament nylon non-absorbable suture.
Apply 100 µL of topical skin adhesive on top of and between skin sutures.
Inject the rat with warm (37 °C) lactated ringer's solution (1CC/100 g BW, SQ) to prevent hypothermia and dehydration.
Inject the rat with buprenorphine (0.5 mg/kg BW, SQ) prior to surgery and every 8 - 12 h for post-op pain relief as needed.
Do not leave the animal unattended until it has regained sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
House the rats individually in separate cages post-surgery.
Place chow soaked in water in a Petri dish on the cage floor for a few days post-op.
Administer carprofen (5 mg/kg BW, SQ) 24 h post-surgery for pain relief every 24 h as needed.
Remove skin sutures while the animal is under 2% isoflurane anesthesia 10 - 14 days post-operation.
Place the osteoporotic rat in the induction chamber attached to an anesthesia machine with a central scavenging system.
Induce anesthesia using 5% isoflurane in 100% oxygen.
Maintain anesthesia via nose cone at 2 - 3% isoflurane.
Scan the rat using an in vivo µCT scanner.
Repeat scanning for longitudinal analysis of bone regeneration.
Ensure all animals are scanned using the same settings.
Contour the vertebra of interest, including all parts while excluding adjacent vertebrae.
Click on "µCT evaluation program" and select the sample from the menu.
Contour each slice using the mouse.
Use the "Z" bar to go to the next slice.
Save the contoured vertebra as a separate file by clicking on "File" → "Save GOBJ" every couple of slices.
Measure the angle of the margins using an XY-slice from the center of the defect for Z-rotation.
Go to the area of the vertebra where the defect is most clear and screen capture the vertebra.
Prepare a rectangle-shaped object in presentation software that will fit into the defect.
Rotate the image of the vertebra such that the defect faces upwards and the defect margins are parallel to the sides of the rectangle.
Measure the angle of rotation by right-clicking on the image → "Format Picture" → "Size".
Use the measured angle to rotate the vertebra.
Open a new DECterm window from "Session manager" → "Applications" → "DECterm".
Run "ipl": Ipl> turn3d -input [in]> -output [out]> -turnaxis_angles [0.000 90.000 90.000]> 90 90 0 -turnangle [0.000]> measured angle -img_interpol_option [1]>
Measure the angle of the margins using a YZ-slice from the center of the defect.
Rotate the vertebra using the measured angle.
Click on "YZ" in "uCT evaluation program".
Define the VOI.
Draw a circular contour of the defect using a slice from the center of the defect.
Copy that contour and paste it on all slices in the defect.
Load the DICOM files of both the target and the reference vertebrae to the main window of the image analysis software.
Register to the reference vertebra.
Launch the "3-D Voxel Registration" module in the software.
Input the reference vertebra as the "Base Volume."
Input the target vertebra as the "Match Volume."
Click "Register" to register the vertebrae.
Save the registered file using the same data type.
Import the registered file into a µCT environment.
Apply the VOI defined for the reference vertebra to the registered target vertebra.
Check that the VOI and defect are concentric.
Send the VOI for evaluation using a µCT evaluation program.
Ensure consistent parameters when analyzing all VOIs.
Set the threshold high enough to omit background noise with minimal loss of bone.
If necessary, segment out radiopaque biomaterial from bone tissue.
Evaluate differences in bone formation between experimental groups qualitatively if needed.
Place the osteoporotic rat in the induction chamber attached to an anesthesia machine.
Induce anesthesia using 5% isoflurane in 100% oxygen.
Maintain anesthesia via nose cone.
Perform euthanasia by incising the chest cavity to produce a bilateral pneumothorax.
